title: ADR 0002 is Accepted and its MVP shipped: the reactor-browser hooks were retyped to a swappable IReactorBrowserClient so a webapp can skip the full reactor
content:
ADR 0002 (**Status: Accepted**, 2026-07-16, decider acaldas) is the decision behind `packages/reactor-browser/src/graphql-client/`. Its own implementation note records that **the MVP shipped**, with batch signing, local-first writes and point-in-time reads deferred.

The context is the problem it removed. `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` shipped **two unrelated ways** for a React app to work with document models:

1. the **full-reactor path** — hooks reading and writing through `window.ph.reactorClient`, an `IReactorClient`, with PGlite, a job queue, the sync manager and its GraphQL channels and a document indexer behind it. Local-first, but heavy; used by Connect and Studio.
2. the **`RemoteDocumentController` path** — a lightweight wrapper around a `PHDocumentController` syncing over plain GraphQL (`MutateDocument` / `GetDocument` / `GetDocumentOperations`), used by a plain webapp (and by `vetra.to`).

The second path had five structural problems that blocked the local-first flow a webapp wants: **no persistence** (state and the pending-action queue lived only in memory, so a refresh lost un-pushed edits), **no offline model** (no reconnect flush, no durable retry), **no shared cache** (two controllers for the same document diverged), **not React friendly** (imperative methods, non-reactive objects), and it **reimplemented sync** on weaker primitives while getting no realtime.

Because both paths duplicated the same concepts — a reducer wrapper, an action tracker, a document cache — in incompatible shapes, a webapp could not adopt `useDocument` / `useDispatch` without adopting the whole reactor. The objective: **one React integration, two interchangeable implementations**, with migration between them a matter of configuration.
